text:
audit-bot: ALERT: Detected public ACL on GCS bucket `redwood-artifacts-prod` (object path: models/2026-03/release.tar.gz). Granter: CI service account. Rule: public-read detected by policy-engine.

kira (sec): on it. can someone confirm scope? public-read on objects or bucket-level?

audit-bot: Finding: OBJECT_ACL public-read on 42 objects, bucket has uniformBucketLevelAccess=OFF. Binding found: allAuthenticatedUsers -> roles/storage.objectViewer via legacy ACL.

samir (infra): wow. CI step probably used `gsutil acl ch -u AllUsers:R` in old deploy job. searching last deploys.

alex (eng-sre): I pulled the auditlog: principal: ci-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com, methodName: storage.objects.update, timestamp: 1745122400. Linked build: build-9923.

maria (platform): temporary containment: I disabled the CI job (build-9923) in Cloud Build and blocked the service account from invoking builds. Can we revert ACLs and rotate any keys used?

kira (sec): containment checklist: 1) remove public ACLs, 2) enable uniform bucket-level access, 3) revoke/grant least-priv SA perms, 4) KMS key policy review, 5) rotate any exposed creds, 6) notify compliance.

samir (infra): running fix now:
```
# remove legacy ACLs from objects (fast path)
for o in $(gsutil ls gs://redwood-artifacts-prod/models/2026-03/**); do
  gsutil acl ch -d AllUsers $o || true
done
# enable uniform bucket-level access
gsutil bucketpolicyonly set on gs://redwood-artifacts-prod
```

alex (eng-sre): heads-up: removing ACLs will break any consumers that rely on object ACLs (shouldn't be any), verifying traces for external public reads last 72h.

kira (sec): also check KMS: are objects encrypted with CMEK? If yes, check key IAM and audit logs for key decrypt requests.

samir (infra): bucket was using CMEK key `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/model-keys/cryptoKeys/model-ck`. Key IAM shows roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter for ci-sa and a broad group `devs@redwood.com` has cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter. That group seems overbroad.

maria (platform): proposed immediate steps: remove AllUsers ACLs (done by samir), set uniform access (done), add conditional IAM on key (restrict to service account + rotate service account if needed), create short-lived signed URLs if external downloads required.

alex (eng-sre): I ran `gsutil ls -L` and confirmed 0 hits for public access after ACL purge. Also started object-level access logs to BigQuery for 90 days.

kira (sec): KMS actions: remove devs@redwood.com role binding on the key, limit to `platform-key-access@redwood` group and CI SA. Also create a key rotation plan (30d) and add audit log alert for cryptoKey.decrypt with anomalous principals.

samir (infra): done: removed devs@redwood.com binding, granted `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to `platform-key-access@redwood` and `ci-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com` only. Also created conditional binding for `platform-key-access@redwood` with request.time < 1748200000 for emergency revert if needed.

kira (sec): we should run a full IAM diff on the project to ensure no other buckets with legacy ACLs or overbroad KMS bindings. alex, can you run the scan?

alex (eng-sre): starting `gcloud asset search-all-resources` + custom script to find uniformBucketLevelAccess=OFF or any ACL grants to AllUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers across projects. ETA ~20m.

maria (platform): communications: I'm drafting an internal incident note for legal/compliance and a short customer-facing blurb in case any artifacts were pulled externally. Need list of exposed object names and public access timestamps. alex, can you dump the access logs and samir the bucket object list with timestamps.

samir (infra): exported object list + ACL change events to gs://redwood-internal-incidents/1745123456/ and shared link: gs://redwood-internal-incidents/1745123456/manifest.csv

alex (eng-sre): access logs show 13 unique external IP GETs to object `models/2026-03/release.tar.gz` between 1745122000 and 1745122400. Looks like crawler hits from 3 ASN ranges. Adding to incident bundle.

kira (sec): action items assigned: samir - rotate CI SA key & audit Cloud Build triggers (done?), alex - run org-wide ACL/KMS scan & export logs, maria - draft comms for compliance, me (kira) - write remediation runbook and postmortem.

samir (infra): rotated CI SA keys, disabled legacy keys, reissued limited SA with new short-lived workload identity binding. Marking builds blocked until testing with new credentials completes.

deploy-bot: Deploy blocked: automatic deployments paused for project redwood-prod until manual approval.

maria (platform): compliance note: logged incident #INC-2026-0312, severity: medium (data exposure of non-PII model artifacts). Notifying privacy and product.

alex (eng-sre): scan results: found 2 other buckets with legacy ACLs in staging; flagged owners and opened PRs to set uniform access and remove ACLs.

kira (sec): post-incident steps: 1) enforce organization policy to block legacy object ACLs (org policy), 2) KMS IAM hygiene checklist + automated alerts, 3) CI/CD lint for gsutil acl usage, 4) run yearly tabletop. I'll attach remediation tasks to the incident.

maria (platform): thanks team. I'll schedule a 1-pager + sync with legal tomorrow 10:00. Any objections to closing the incident after 72h of stable logs?

samir (infra): no objections. recommend 7-day monitoring window for crawlers.

kira (sec): agreed. Keeping incident open for 7 days, will move to postmortem draft in #postmortems once we have all artifacts. :white_check_mark:

alex (eng-sre): closing actions: PRs for bucket policy changes, KMS IAM update tracked in repo infra/iam#452, incident bundle uploaded to gs://redwood-internal-incidents/1745123456/bundle.tar.gz

maria (platform): ping if you need anything else, closing thread here.
